docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: • The purpose of this datasheet is to show my details of my subsystem, and how it works in synch with my team HaMaLoYa's overall device.

docs.title: Project Summary
docs.text:
• My subsystem is an audio speaker that will work with the team project. My work will contribute to the overall success of this device by receiving a signal from Logan Maeltsrom's device, and will react by emmitting an noise from a speaker to alert the user of the device to stay awake. The user will then have to manually turn off the noise by pressing a button, that way it makes sure that the user is awake and aware.
  • As you look through my subsystem, you may take a look how it works together with my teams overall design by using this link: team report.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This block diagram is an overview of my individual subsystem, the components used, and electrical connections. My subsystem will use the PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano to control the speaker circuitry, debug red LED, and inputs. I also added a 5V regulator power level. My connector will receive a signal from Logan's connector 3 pin 2, into my connector 1 pin 2.

docs.text: This block diagram shows my individual subsystem set up that includes the PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano, transistor circuitry, a speaker, the connection to my teammate Logan's subsystem and more.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This schematic is designed to support the overall function of our product by reacting to Logan Maeltsrom's board. My board will be a subsystem for triggering an audio alarm through a speaker to alert the driver. My power supply circuitry includes 5V regulator with a barrel jack that will be receiving a DC of 9V. I also have a speaker circuitry that includes transistors and headers to allow the speaker to be removable. Lastly, I have a nano PIC board that will be receiving Logan's command as mentioned before. I included extra header pins for ground, power and GPIO pins for back up. I also included a debugging button and red LED, as well a speaker button to turn it on and off.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A power budget was done as it was very useful in allowing me to estimate the amount of power my subsystem needs to work. I started off my listing the major components used in my subsystem. I listed each components supply voltage and maximum current the component can consume. We were advised to add a 25% safety margin as a buffer to allow a bit more current capability to the subsystem.

docs.title: Conclusions
docs.text: From the prepared Power Budget, I found that the total estimated current with the 25% safety margin, comes out to 964 mA. Therefore, I am within the range of an assumed 1000mA capacity for the 5V voltage regulator chosen for this subsystem.
